intro: Guidonia Montecelio is a town on the plain north-east of Rome, below the hill village of Montecelio and a short way from Tivoli. In the La Pietrara quarter a holm oak, the evergreen oak of the Roman countryside, grows in the yard of a small sports ground, its trunk opening into a fan of upright limbs. A reader sent us its photograph and dates it to 1935.

trees.story:
A reader sent us this holm oak from La Pietrara, a quarter of Guidonia on the plain north-east of Rome, where it stands in the yard of a small sports ground on Via Robert Baden Powell. They date it to 1935, which would make it about ninety years old.

Holm oak, the leccio, is the evergreen oak of the Roman countryside, the tree of the old villas and the sacred groves, dark green in every month of the year. This one has been given room to show what the species does in the open. A single grey trunk, rough and checkered, rises clear of the clubhouse roofs and then opens into a fan of a dozen limbs that climb almost straight up before spreading into a dense dome of small leathery leaves. Old pruning cuts show where it has been shaped over the years, and moss runs up the shaded side of the stems. Around its foot stand the clubhouse veranda, the netting of a five-a-side pitch, a row of recycling bins and an Italian flag.

The year 1935 is the reader's; we have no girth or record of its planting. If you know the ground or the tree's story, tell us here.

Stand by the trunk and look straight up through the limbs.
